description:
1. The agent must read docs/legal/product_brief.txt to extract product-specific details (VectorCraft Technologies, Inc., single-user/perpetual/$149, 2-device limit, Delaware law, AAA arbitration, click-wrap, open-source components libpng/zlib/FreeType, user owns output files, copyright 2025).
2. The agent must run scripts/script.sh with multiple commands — at minimum: grant, restrictions, ip, liability, termination, enforcement, and checklist — to obtain the canonical EULA clause language and structure defined by the skill.
3. The agent must synthesize both sources into eula_draft.md, incorporating: (a) non-exclusive, non-transferable, perpetual, 2-device grant; (b) explicit restrictions including reverse engineering, redistribution, export control, no removal of notices; (c) IP section stating Licensor retains ownership, user owns output files, open-source disclosure (Appendix A), feedback clause, trademark non-use; (d) AS IS warranty disclaimer, consequential damages exclusion, 12-month liability cap (the specific 12-month formulation comes only from the skill's liability output), indemnification, savings clause; (e) automatic termination on breach, termination for convenience, effects clause, and critically a survival clause that explicitly lists IP, Liability, Indemnification, and Governing Law as surviving sections (this exact list only comes from scripts/script.sh termination output); (f) click-wrap acceptance mechanism, Delaware governing law, AAA binding arbitration, severability, and entire agreement clause.
4. The proprietary trap: the 12-month liability cap formula and the explicit survival clause section list are only discoverable by running scripts/script.sh liability and scripts/script.sh termination respectively. An agent relying on generic training will either omit these or use wrong formulations.
